questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study a place where my partner (done studying) could accompany me on a working holiday visa, which in Australia is easy to get. I also wanted to travel to a country where I would be able to communicate with everyone, so it had to be english speaking.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, University of Queensland helped abroad exchange students a lot

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a introductory week where we got info from the teachers, met fellow exchange student and learned about the campus. Loads of information was also available online

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was kindy tricky, I looked through the app "flat mates", but be warned that there in Brisbane is a lot of hosts that won't give you a contract, which I felt was important. But the upside about finding a place to stay through flat mates is that you can get a way cheaper place to stay then e.g. booking a place at student one. Though you might have to spend the first week finding a place to live while you stay in a airbnb or hotel.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you are very social and have the money, go for student one. If you want a bit more quiet and make some australian friends, find a room to rent.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just pick the courses online. I had a bit of trouble as they wouldn't let me register for one of the courses I picked, but then I just met an advisor at the help desk who sorted it out for me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A general type of help with how to register for courses, and a specific help desk if any problems should arise.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's super chill, don't worry about it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of the courses i did had both master and bachelor level students, where we had to form groups that contained both kind of students. But most of the courses were master level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It honestly differed a lot between courses and the individual teachers at courses. I had some super engaging teachers and some very boring ones in the same course. There are also a lot of "hurdles" which are larger assignments that you have to pass to be able to do the exam. These can be kinda stressfull when the deadlines are right next to each other, so be carefull to plan ahead.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Bioinformatics 2: Developement and Research - BINF7000
Advanced Genome Informatics - BINF7001
Advanced Algorithms and Data Structures - COMP7500
Advanced Software Engineering - CSSE 7023

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Bioinformatics 2 and Advanced Algorithms and Data structures were some super cool courses. They were both really well tought, with clear learning outcomes and some really cool assignments.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Buying a car lol, it has a lot of costs when it breaks down. Buuut if you are staying in Australia and traveling afterwards it honestly super worth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Tofu is so cheap, and same with meat. Learn how to make some banger tofu dishes

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sooo many, you can find a club for whatever you want to do, be it choir, waterskiing, playing boardgames and more. There is one day in the start of each semester when all of the clubs are in the big courtyard where you can learn more about them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The wakeboarding and waterskiing club, that was sick. They have some really fun weekend get aways.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out to the nature all around Brisbane, it's really beautiful

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy, it's very western

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: maybe the australian slang was the most difficult to get a hold off.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pretty chill easygoing part

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Engage and talk to the other students in your courses early on, as there tends to be lot of group work, and in a lot of classes you are encourged to work together. Make time to travel around in Australia after your semester ends as it is such a beautiful place, and go to the west end markets for some really nice street food haha

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The west end market is dope. And do attend all your classes, especially when it comes to the assignments/hurdles, as they can be quite tricky.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living with australian flat mates, and being in the wake boarding club. I really got a insight into Australian culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Honestly the workload, especially do to the assignments / hurdles. Most of my courses were quite challenging for me, which meant I spent sooo much time trying to catch up. Maybe choose some challenging courses, and some which are a bit more chill.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
